question:
Choose the idiom/phrase that can substitute the highlighted group of words meaningfully.

Her wedding is **occurring soon**, and she is so nervous about it.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Just around the corner"** refers to something **that is going to happen very soon.** (बहुत जल्द होने वाला)

 
 
• **Example: **With the holidays **just around the corner**, everyone is in a festive mood.
 
 
 
• Hence, the phrase that meaningfully substitutes the highlighted group of words "occurring soon" is **"Just around the corner"**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **In hot water** (मुसीबत में होना): To be in trouble or experiencing difficulties.

 
 
• **Example:** He found himself in hot water after missing the important meeting.
 
 
 
• **Through thick and thin** (हर परिस्थिति में साथ देना): To support someone in both good and bad times.
 
 
• **Example:** They have remained friends through thick and thin.
 
 
 
• **In the dark** (अनजान होना): To be unaware of something.
 
 
• **Example:** I'm completely in the dark about the new project details.
